findings: The selected THK HSR12XRM candidate is factually ready for representative construction. Official THK instructions require a removing/mounting jig, full end-face contact, parallel insertion, and discontinuation of use after rolling-element loss.

Primary THK catalog page images independently verify the essential mechanism: four recirculating ball rows, 45-degree contact, end-plate circulation, and the explicit exclusion of HSR8X/10X/12X from retained-ball models.

The model-specific drawings consistently establish HSR12XRM dimensions in millimetres: 20 mm block height, 27 mm width, 45 mm length, 12 mm rail width, and 11 mm rail height. No HSR15 geometry is mixed into the current candidate.

The plan appropriately treats ball diameter/count, race microprofile, jig length, clearance, transfer-gap tolerance, and angular tolerance as disclosed prototype assumptions rather than THK specifications. It preserves independent rigid balls, four physical circulation paths, continuous rail-to-jig support, and actual contact physics.

The proposed pre-YAM tests cover circulation and loss, gap and inclination sensitivity, timestep stability, contact-force limits, reset freshness, and deliberate misalignment. Direct pose/velocity writes, fixed balls, hidden welds, and collision suppression are explicitly prohibited.

Three genuinely distinct sourced objectives were considered. The ABB deformable DressPack candidate and Dell ReadyRails candidate are correctly withheld because their essential physics or retention geometry remains unsupported; only the THK rigid-body candidate is marked ready.

The previous ambiguous-selection failure is resolved by the acquired, model-specific manufacturer structure and dimensional evidence. Novelty remains a separate subsequent gate and is not asserted here.

artifacts/candidate-preflight.json is historical and unrelated to this selection, while artifacts/candidate-critic.json records the earlier deficiencies that the current candidates and selected artifacts now address; neither stale artifact was used as affirmative evidence.
